primary_text: One of the first lessons in jiu-jitsu is not how to win. It is how to communicate and respect a boundary. At Joao Crus BJJ, Youth ages 8–12 practice tapping, stopping when a partner taps, resetting, and trying again with a coach. See the Austin class inside Castle Hill Fitness.
headline: Tap Means Stop

primary_text: Confidence does not have to come before the first class. It can grow when a child gets stuck, listens to coaching, tries again, and sees progress. Austin Youth BJJ is built for ages 8–12, including complete beginners.
headline: Confidence Is Practiced

primary_text: Central Austin parents: Youth BJJ for ages 8–12 is coming inside Castle Hill Fitness. Tuesday and Thursday, 5:00–5:45 p.m. Answer a few practical questions, then Joao personally calls to plan a free studio visit.
headline: Youth BJJ in Central Austin

primary_text: You do not need to get in shape before starting jiu-jitsu. You need a place where beginner questions are expected and the first step is clear. Adult group classes meet Tue/Thu from 6:00–7:00 p.m. inside Castle Hill Fitness.
headline: New to Jiu-Jitsu? Start Here.

primary_text: Pressure is part of training. Panic does not have to control the response. Adult BJJ gives you a place to practice position, timing, breathing, and technical decisions with coaching. Train Tue/Thu inside Castle Hill Fitness.
headline: Practice Calm Under Pressure

primary_text: Some adults want a consistent group. Others need focused coaching around a schedule, injury history, or technical goal. Austin offers group classes Tue/Thu from 6:00–7:00 p.m. plus private lessons by appointment. Use the finder to choose a starting point.
headline: Group or Private? Find Your Fit.
